title: SQL CASE Expression
text:
SQL
CASE
Expression



The SQL CASE Expression

The
CASE
expression is used to define
different results based on specified conditions in an SQL statement.

The
CASE
expression goes through the conditions and
stops at the first match (like an if-then-else statement). So, once a condition is true, it will stop
processing and return the result. If no conditions are true, it returns
the value in the
ELSE
clause. If there is no
ELSE

clause and no conditions are true, it returns NULL.

CASE Syntax

CASE

WHEN
condition1
THEN
result1

WHEN
condition2
THEN
result2

WHEN
conditionN
THEN
resultN

ELSE
default_result

END;
